- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates or spikes too early; reduce initial forecast peaks and add lagged smoothing.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 3x recent mean), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at 2x recent high or apply exponential decay.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3 days, model often fails to adjust; force mean reversion toward recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model exhibits strong overconfidence in early days (days 1–5); scale down early forecast values by 20–40% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00/1.00 extremes, model tends to misread momentum; use sentiment-weighted moving average for smoothing.
